requirements.quote: Header Form (1) = 1,
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Header Form field is one bit and has the fixed value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A long header packet must not encode the Header Form field as 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and fixed value can be checked directly in the first byte.

requirements.quote: Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
requirements.condition: When encoding the generic long-header structure shown in Figure 13.
requirements.required_behavior: The Fixed Bit is one bit and has the value 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and value are directly observable in an encoded header.

requirements.quote: Long Packet Type (2),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Long Packet Type field occupies two bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field width can be verified at the bit level.

requirements.quote: Type-Specific Bits (4),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Type-Specific Bits field occupies four bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field width can be verified at the bit level.

requirements.quote: Version (32),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Version field occupies 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field width can be verified directly.

requirements.quote:
Destination Connection ID Length (8),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Destination Connection ID Length field occupies 8 bits, and the Destination Connection ID occupies from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Both field widths are mechanically observable in packet bytes.

requirements.quote:
Source Connection ID Length (8),
     Source Connection ID (0..160),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The Source Connection ID Length field occupies 8 bits, and the Source Connection ID occupies from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Both field widths are mechanically observable in packet bytes.

requirements.quote: Type-Specific Payload (..),
requirements.condition: When a long header packet contains bytes after its header fields.
requirements.required_behavior: Those remaining bytes form a variable-length Type-Specific Payload.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser can identify whether trailing bytes are assigned to the type-specific payload.

requirements.quote:
establishment of 1-RTT keys.  Once 1-RTT keys are available, a sender
   switches to sending packets using the short header (Section 17.3).
requirements.condition: Once a sender has 1-RTT keys available.
requirements.required_behavior: The sender switches to sending packets with the short header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender must not continue selecting the long header for ordinary packet sending after 1-RTT keys become available.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can make 1-RTT keys available and observe the header form selected for subsequent packets.

requirements.quote:
Header Form:  The most significant bit (0x80) of byte 0 (the first
      byte) is set to 1 for long headers.
requirements.condition: When a packet uses a long header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the most significant bit, mask 0x80, of byte 0 to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a long header with the most significant bit of byte 0 cleared.
requirements.why_checkable: The specified bit can be inspected directly in byte 0.

requirements.quote:
Fixed Bit:  The next bit (0x40) of byte 0 is set to 1, unless the
      packet is a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.condition: When encoding a long-header packet other than a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set bit 0x40 of byte 0 to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not clear bit 0x40 for a non-Version-Negotiation long-header packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet type and bit 0x40 are directly observable in an encoded packet.

requirements.quote:
packet is a Version Negotiation packet.  Packets containing a zero
      value for this bit are not valid packets in this version and MUST
      be discarded.
requirements.condition: When receiving a packet in QUIC version 1 whose Fixed Bit is zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or process the packet as a valid version 1 packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted packet with bit 0x40 cleared can be supplied and its rejection observed.

requirements.quote:
Long Packet Type:  The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x30) of
      byte 0 contain a packet type.  Packet types are listed in Table 5.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or read the packet type in the two bits selected by mask 0x30 of byte 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type bit position and width can be verified from byte 0.

requirements.quote:
Type-Specific Bits:  The semantics of the lower four bits (those with
      a mask of 0x0f) of byte 0 are determined by the packet type.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the lower four bits of byte 0 in a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the bits selected by mask 0x0f according to the packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply packet-type-independent semantics to these four bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary the packet type and verify that the same bit positions receive the corresponding type-specific interpretation.

requirements.quote:
Version:  The QUIC Version is a 32-bit field that follows the first
      byte.  This field indicates the version of QUIC that is in use and
      determines how the rest of the protocol fields are interpreted.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place a 32-bit Version field immediately after byte 0 and interpret the remaining protocol fields according to that version.
requirements.why_checkable: The field position and width are directly observable, and version-dependent parser selection can be exercised.

requirements.quote:
Destination Connection ID Length:  The byte following the version
      contains the length in bytes of the Destination Connection ID
      field that follows it.  This length is encoded as an 8-bit
      unsigned integer.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place an 8-bit unsigned Destination Connection ID length immediately after the Version field; its value gives the following Destination Connection ID length in bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The length byte, its position, and agreement with the following field can be verified from packet bytes.

requirements.quote:
unsigned integer.  In QUIC version 1, this value MUST NOT exceed
      20 bytes.
requirements.condition: When encoding a QUIC version 1 long header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a Destination Connection ID length no greater than 20 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Destination Connection ID length greater than 20 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The one-byte length value can be compared with the bound of 20.

requirements.quote:
20 bytes.  Endpoints that receive a version 1 long header with a
      value larger than 20 MUST drop the packet.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a QUIC version 1 long header with a Destination Connection ID length greater than 20.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or continue processing the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet declaring a length above 20 can be injected and packet dropping observed.

requirements.quote:
form a Version Negotiation packet, servers SHOULD be able to read
      longer connection IDs from other QUIC versions.
requirements.condition: When a server reads a long-header packet from another QUIC version in order to form a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Be able to read connection IDs longer than the QUIC version 1 limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A server can be given an other-version packet containing a connection ID longer than 20 bytes and tested for successful reading.

requirements.quote:
Destination Connection ID:  The Destination Connection ID field
      follows the Destination Connection ID Length field, which
      indicates the length of this field.  Section 7.2 describes the use
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Destination Connection ID in a long header.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Destination Connection ID immediately after its length field and make its byte length equal the value indicated by that field.
requirements.why_checkable: Field ordering and correspondence between declared and actual length are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Source Connection ID Length:  The byte following the Destination
      Connection ID contains the length in bytes of the Source
      Connection ID field that follows it.  This length is encoded as an
      8-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place an 8-bit unsigned Source Connection ID length immediately after the Destination Connection ID; its value gives the following Source Connection ID length in bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The length byte, its position, and agreement with the following field can be verified from packet bytes.

requirements.quote:
8-bit unsigned integer.  In QUIC version 1, this value MUST NOT
      exceed 20 bytes.
requirements.condition: When encoding a QUIC version 1 long header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a Source Connection ID length no greater than 20 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Source Connection ID length greater than 20 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The one-byte length value can be compared with the bound of 20.

requirements.quote:
exceed 20 bytes.  Endpoints that receive a version 1 long header
      with a value larger than 20 MUST drop the packet.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a QUIC version 1 long header with a Source Connection ID length greater than 20.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or continue processing the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet declaring a length above 20 can be injected and packet dropping observed.

requirements.quote:
properly form a Version Negotiation packet, servers SHOULD be able
      to read longer connection IDs from other QUIC versions.
requirements.condition: When a server reads a long-header packet from another QUIC version in order to form a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Be able to read connection IDs longer than the QUIC version 1 limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A server can be given an other-version packet containing a connection ID longer than 20 bytes and tested for successful reading.

requirements.quote:
Source Connection ID:  The Source Connection ID field follows the
      Source Connection ID Length field, which indicates the length of
      this field.  Section 7.2 describes the use of this field in more
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Source Connection ID in a long header.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Source Connection ID immediately after its length field and make its byte length equal the value indicated by that field.
requirements.why_checkable: Field ordering and correspondence between declared and actual length are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Type-Specific Payload:  The remainder of the packet, if any, is type
      specific.
requirements.condition: When bytes remain after the preceding long-header fields.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the remainder as payload specific to the packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser's assignment and interpretation of trailing bytes can be observed for each packet type.

requirements.quote: | 0x00 | Initial   | Section 17.2.2 |
requirements.condition: When the two-bit long packet type value is 0x00 in QUIC version 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the packet as an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type value can be mapped to the parser's selected packet type.

requirements.quote: | 0x01 | 0-RTT     | Section 17.2.3 |
requirements.condition: When the two-bit long packet type value is 0x01 in QUIC version 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the packet as a 0-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type value can be mapped to the parser's selected packet type.

requirements.quote: | 0x02 | Handshake | Section 17.2.4 |
requirements.condition: When the two-bit long packet type value is 0x02 in QUIC version 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the packet as a Handshake packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type value can be mapped to the parser's selected packet type.

requirements.quote: | 0x03 | Retry     | Section 17.2.5 |
requirements.condition: When the two-bit long packet type value is 0x03 in QUIC version 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the packet as a Retry packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type value can be mapped to the parser's selected packet type.

requirements.quote:
The header form bit, Destination and Source Connection ID lengths,
   Destination and Source Connection ID fields, and Version fields of a
   long header packet are version independent.  The other fields in the
   first byte are version specific.
requirements.condition: When parsing long-header packets across QUIC versions.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the Header Form bit, both Connection ID length fields, both Connection ID fields, and Version field as version-independent; interpret the other first-byte fields according to the version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make the identified invariant fields version-specific or treat the other first-byte fields as invariant across versions.
requirements.why_checkable: Multi-version parser tests can verify invariant extraction of the listed fields and version-selected handling of the remaining first-byte fields.

requirements.quote:
The interpretation of the fields and the payload are specific to a
   version and packet type.
requirements.condition: When interpreting long-header fields and payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Select their interpretation using both the QUIC version and packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary version and packet type and observe the selected decoding path.

requirements.quote:
Reserved Bits:  Two bits (those with a mask of 0x0c) of byte 0 are
      reserved across multiple packet types.
requirements.condition: For long-header packet types that contain the shared Reserved Bits.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the two bits selected by mask 0x0c of byte 0 as Reserved Bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The reserved bit positions and width are directly inspectable in byte 0.

requirements.quote:
reserved across multiple packet types.  These bits are protected
      using header protection; see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When transmitting or receiving a long-header packet type containing the Reserved Bits.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply header protection to the Reserved Bits on transmission and remove it before evaluating their protected value on receipt.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet bytes before and after header protection can be compared to verify that mask 0x0c participates in protection processing.

requirements.quote:
using header protection; see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The value
      included prior to protection MUST be set to 0.
requirements.condition: Before applying header protection to a packet containing the Reserved Bits.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Reserved Bits value to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a non-zero value in the Reserved Bits before protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The unprotected header produced by the sender can be inspected for mask 0x0c equal to zero.

requirements.quote:
included prior to protection MUST be set to 0.  An endpoint MUST
      treat receipt of a packet that has a non-zero value for these bits
      after removing both packet and header protection as a connection
      error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: After an endpoint has removed both packet protection and header protection and the Reserved Bits are non-zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not silently accept or merely discard the packet.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A protected packet that reveals non-zero reserved bits after both protection layers are removed can be injected and the connection error type observed.

requirements.quote:
error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  Discarding such a packet after
      only removing header protection can expose the endpoint to
      attacks; see Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When header protection has been removed from a packet whose Reserved Bits appear non-zero but packet protection has not yet been removed.
requirements.required_behavior: Defer the reserved-bit validity decision until packet protection has also been removed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the packet solely after removing header protection based on the apparent Reserved Bits value.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can verify that reserved-bit rejection occurs only after both protection layers have been removed.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number Length:  In packet types that contain a Packet Number
      field, the least significant two bits (those with a mask of 0x03)
      of byte 0 contain the length of the Packet Number field, encoded
      as an unsigned two-bit integer that is one less than the length of
      the Packet Number field in bytes.
requirements.condition: When a long-header packet type contains a Packet Number field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode its length in the least significant two bits of byte 0, mask 0x03, as an unsigned two-bit value equal to the Packet Number field byte length minus one.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-bit value can be compared directly with the actual Packet Number field length.

requirements.quote:
the Packet Number field in bytes.  That is, the length of the
      Packet Number field is the value of this field plus one.
requirements.condition: When decoding the Packet Number Length bits of a packet type containing a Packet Number field.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute the Packet Number field length in bytes as the encoded two-bit value plus one.
requirements.why_checkable: For each two-bit value from 0 through 3, the resulting length can be checked as 1 through 4 bytes.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number field is the value of this field plus one.  These
      bits are protected using header protection; see Section 5.4 of
      [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When transmitting or receiving a packet whose first byte contains Packet Number Length bits.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply header protection to the Packet Number Length bits on transmission and remove header protection before decoding them on receipt.
requirements.why_checkable: Protected and unprotected first-byte values can be compared to verify protection processing of mask 0x03.
